title: Attention-chunk handoff orchestrator for async NCCL handoff and kernel hinting
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce end-to-end prefill+decode latency and increase aggregate throughput for multi-GPU tensor/pipeline setups by introducing an attention-chunk handoff orchestrator that coordinates chunked attention computation, kernel-selection hints, and asynchronous NCCL handoffs between stages.

Background: In current multi-GPU prefill/decode flows we observe stalls caused by long attention kernels blocking NCCL windows and suboptimal kernel selection for variable chunk shapes. This leads to underutilized comm overlap and higher p99 latency for medium-length prompts.

Proposal: Implement an orchestrator that: 1) dynamically shards attention into chunk windows (configurable min/max chunk sizes), 2) emits kernel-hint metadata to the runtime kernel selector to prefer low-latency kernels for the head/tail chunks and throughput kernels for steady-state chunks, 3) schedules asynchronous NCCL handoff windows so communication can proceed while remaining compute overlap finishes, and 4) provides deterministic fallbacks for single-GPU and heterogeneous device groups.

Key design points:
- Chunking heuristic: hybrid of token-count and compute-cost estimate (FLOPs proxy) with hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- Kernel hint API: lightweight per-chunk tags ("latency_peak", "throughput_steady", "kv_prefetch") consumed by kernel selector to bias kernel and tile choices.
- NCCL handoff: orchestrator issues a non-blocking notify to comm-subsystem when a chunk's KV set is ready, allowing receiver-side to begin async recv while sender finishes remaining compute. Handshake includes epoch token to preserve ordering.
- Correctness: preserve deterministic attention outputs when running with deterministic kernels; provide reconciliation step for non-deterministic fast-paths.
- Metrics/tracing: per-chunk timing, NCCL overlap ratio, kernel selection counts, and per-request tail latency.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end p99 latency reduction >= 10% for 64-512 token prompts on benchmark models (tested on 4xA100 and mixed A100/A10G setups).
- Throughput increase >= 12% under steady-state multi-tenant load.
- No correctness regressions vs baseline deterministic path (bitwise-equal) for enabled test harness.
- New kernel-hint API documented and feature-flagged (default off).

Artifacts/links: 
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/display/RT/Attention+Chunk+Handoff+Orchestrator
- Design diagram: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1AttnChunkDesign
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7981 (WIP)
- Perf dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.net/d/attn-chunk/attn-chunk-perf

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: handshake overhead cancels NCCL overlap gains. Mitigation: microbenchmarks for handshake latency; coalesce small chunk handoffs.
- Risk: kernel hint mis-biases selection causing throughput regression. Mitigation: A/B rollout with canary and automatic rollback rule if unit-economics degrade >5%.
- Risk: heterogeneous GPU driver behaviors. Mitigation: device-profiled default chunk sizes and explicit slow-device blacklisting.
